He was previously a correspondent for the Financial Times and BBC News. Provide news feedback or report an error. ## **Takeaways** by Bloomberg AI. A profile-cum-investigation of Sam Altman in *The New Yorker* drilled deep into the OpenAI chief executive officer’s personality foibles, to put it midly, as he steers the AI firm to an initial public offering that may value the company at more than $1 trillion. The takeaway is that even though the documents governing the IPO are unlikely to mention it, one of the biggest so-called risk factors facing the company is Altman himself. Average deal size climbed to $36.7 million, the highest average Rock Health has tracked in a single quarter since Q4 2021, according to the company's Q1 digital health funding recap report. items.raw_snippet: # Alibaba creates CEO-led technology committee amid intensifying AI race. Chinese e-commerce and AI giant Alibaba Group Holding has set up a high-level technology committee led by CEO Eddie Wu Yongming, as part of a broader restructuring to sharpen its focus on artificial intelligence amid intensifying competition. The Hangzhou-based company formed the Alibaba Group Technology Committee as part of its efforts to accelerate AI development, according to an internal letter from Wu to staff on Wednesday. The committee brings together several senior executives, including Zhou Jingren, the former chief technology officer of Alibaba Cloud, who will serve as its chief AI architect. Group CTO Wu Zeming will focus on the company’s business technology and AI inference platforms, after previously leading its food delivery operations. The restructuring follows the recent creation of the Alibaba Token Hub (ATH) Business Group, which consolidates the company’s core AI teams and products. items.raw_snippet: # The New Survival Skill: Build Like a Polymath, Lead Like a CEO. To lead, not just survive but thrive, you must become an AI-driven entrepreneurial polymath. Some entrepreneurs dedicate their lives to building and scaling a single enterprise, but the most impactful among them — entrepreneurial polymaths (or serial entrepreneurs) — never stop creating. In an entrepreneurial context, a polymath entrepreneur blends adaptability and insatiable curiosity with the commercial instincts to turn knowledge and innovation into enterprises. Entrepreneurs often have blind spots in the disciplines of management, strategy, innovation management, implementation, culture, resource allocation, productivity and sustainable value creation. Bottom line: The most successful will be those who will be applying the fast-evolving tools of AI to not just innovate and add new value through the optimization of your organization but also to create new solutions for your customer/market that innovate your industry — and often will create a new sustainable business faster and more value-creating than ever before.
